title: Descript Alternatives in 2026: Free and Paid Tools Compared
summary: The best Descript alternatives in 2026 for screen recordings, podcasts and video editing: Tella, Riverside, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, ScreenPal, iMovie and OBS Studio, with current pricing and what each does better or worse than Descript.
body_markdown:
[Descript](https://www.tella.com/blog/what-is-descript) made[text-based video editing](https://www.tella.com/blog/descript-video-editing-how-does-it-work) mainstream: you edit a video by editing its transcript. It's still a strong tool, but people look for alternatives when they only need part of it, want a simpler way to record and share screen videos, or want something free.


This guide groups the alternatives by the job you're doing, so you can skip the ones that don't fit.


Disclosure: we make Tella, and it's first on the list. Competitor pricing and features come from each vendor's own website, last checked on October 19, 2026, and linked below. Prices change, so check the vendor's page before you buy.


## The short answer


- **For screen recordings, demos and tutorials:**[Tella](https://www.tella.com/) records your screen and camera, lets you cut by transcript, and shares the result as a link or embed.
- **For remote podcasts and interviews:**[Riverside](https://riverside.com/pricing) records each guest on a separate track and has text-based editing.
- **For free editing with a transcript:**[CapCut](https://www.capcut.com/tools/desktop-video-editor) desktop has transcript-based editing and auto captions.
- **For a free professional editor:**[DaVinci Resolve](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve) is free on Mac, Windows and Linux.
- **For free recording only:**[OBS Studio](https://obsproject.com/) is free and open source.

## Why people look for a Descript alternative


- **They mostly record their screen.** Descript has a screen recorder, but it's one part of a big editor built around podcasts and production. If most of your videos are demos, walkthroughs or tutorials, a screen recorder with editing and sharing built in is faster.
- **Media hours and AI credits.** Every Descript plan includes a monthly allowance: 10 media hours and 400 AI credits on Hobbyist, 30 media hours and 800 AI credits on Creator, and 40 media hours and 1,500 AI credits on Business. Heavy users buy top-ups.
- **They want something free.** Descript's free plan is for trying it out. Free editors such as CapCut, DaVinci Resolve and iMovie have no media-hour allowance.


## Screen recordings, demos and tutorials


### 1. Tella


[Tella](https://www.tella.com/) is a screen recorder for polished product demos, tutorials and async video. You record your screen and camera, edit in the browser, and share a link or embed.


**Where it matches Descript:**


- [Edit by transcript](https://www.tella.com/help/editing/edit-the-transcript-of-a-tella-video) : select words in the Script panel to cut them, keep a section, or copy it to a new clip.
- [Remove filler words and silences](https://www.tella.com/auto-cut) in one click each.
- [Studio Voice](https://www.tella.com/studio-voice) removes background noise and evens out your voice.
- The[Tella Agent](https://www.tella.com/help/editing/edit-with-the-tella-agent) , in public beta on paid plans, edits your video from a chat message: cuts, layouts, zooms and subtitles.


**Where it's different:**


- Built for screen and camera recordings, with a Mac app, a Windows app (in beta), a Chrome extension and a web recorder.
- Sharing is built in: every video gets a share page and an embeddable player, and you can[publish to YouTube and other social platforms](https://www.tella.com/help/sharing/publish-to-social-media) .
- You can't reword the transcript to regenerate speech, as Descript's AI voice tools can.


**Pricing:** a 7-day free trial of Pro with no credit card, then[Pro at $13 per user per month](https://www.tella.com/pricing) billed annually ($26 monthly) or Premium at $19 ($39 monthly). There is no permanently free plan.


**Best for:** founders, product and marketing teams, and educators who record demos and tutorials.


### 2. ScreenPal


[ScreenPal](https://screenpal.com/plans) , formerly Screencast-O-Matic, is a screen recorder and video editor popular in education. It works on Windows, Mac, Chromebook, iOS and Android.


**Pricing:** a free plan with a 15-minute recording limit and 10 hosted videos. Deluxe is $4 a month and Max, which adds AI captions and transcriptions, is $10 a month, both billed annually.


**Best for:** teachers and anyone who needs simple, low-cost screen recordings.


## Podcasts and interviews


### 3. Riverside


[Riverside](https://riverside.com/pricing) is a recording studio for remote podcasts, interviews and webinars, with an AI, text-based editor. It records each participant on a separate track.


**Pricing:** a free plan that includes 2 hours of separate-track recording (one-off). Pro is $24 a month billed annually ($29 monthly) with a 14-day free trial.


**Best for:** podcasters and anyone recording guests remotely, which is the main thing people use Descript for besides editing.


## Free video editors


### 4. CapCut


[CapCut](https://www.capcut.com/tools/desktop-video-editor) has a desktop video editor for Windows 7 or later and macOS 10.14 or later, with templates, effects, auto captions and transcript-based editing.


**Pricing:** the desktop editor is free to download; paid plans add AI features and credits.


**Best for:** social video for TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts.


### 5. DaVinci Resolve


[DaVinci Resolve](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve) from Blackmagic Design combines editing, color correction, visual effects and audio post-production, for Mac, Windows and Linux.


**Pricing:** free. DaVinci Resolve Studio is a one-time $295.


**Best for:** editors who want professional tools without a subscription and are happy to learn a timeline editor.


### 6. Apple iMovie


[iMovie](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/imovie/id408981434) is Apple's free video editor for the Mac.


**Pricing:** free on the Mac App Store.


**Best for:** beginners on a Mac who need simple cuts, titles and music.


## Free recording only


### 7. OBS Studio


[OBS Studio](https://obsproject.com/) is free and open-source software for video recording and live streaming on Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or later, and Linux. It has no editor, transcript or hosting, so you'll pair it with one of the editors above.


**Best for:** gamers, streamers and anyone who wants free, unlimited recording.


## Questions people ask


### What is the best alternative to Descript?


It depends on what you use Descript for. For screen recordings, product demos and tutorials, Tella records your screen and camera, edits by transcript and shares a link. For remote podcasts and interviews, Riverside records each guest on a separate track and has text-based editing. For free editing, CapCut has transcript-based editing and DaVinci Resolve is a free professional editor.


### Is there a free alternative to Descript?


Yes. CapCut's desktop editor, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie and OBS Studio are free to download, and ScreenPal and Riverside have free plans with limits. Descript also has its own free plan. Tella has a 7-day free trial rather than a free plan.


### How much does Descript cost?


As of October 2026, Descript has a free plan, and paid plans per person per month of $16 for Hobbyist, $24 for Creator and $50 for Business billed annually, or $24, $35 and $65 billed monthly ([Descript pricing](https://www.descript.com/pricing) ).


### Is Tella cheaper than Descript?


Tella Pro is $13 per user per month billed annually ($26 monthly), compared with $16 for Descript Hobbyist and $24 for Creator. Tella has no free plan, but every new workspace gets a 7-day free trial of Pro without a card.


### Which Descript alternatives have text-based editing?


Tella, Riverside and CapCut. In Tella you select words in the transcript to cut them; you can't reword the transcript to regenerate speech.


## Summing it up


Pick the alternative that matches the job: Tella for screen recordings and demos you want to share, Riverside for remote podcasts, CapCut or DaVinci Resolve for free editing, and OBS Studio for free recording. For a closer look at how Tella and Descript compare, see[Tella vs Descript](https://www.tella.com/alternatives/descript) .
